diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that part (iii) of \Cref{thm:hs_frac_charac} is precisely the statement of \Cref{thm:diff_density_hs_invariance}.
Assume that $\calK \in L(C_b, C_b)$ and that \eqref{e:hl_charac} is satisfied for some $\ell \in \bN$ with $\ell > \sigma_{n,l}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:diff_density_hs_invariance is stated without condition (L1), yet its only proof is 'follows from' thm:hs_frac_charac(iii), whose standing hypothesis is (L1) (needed for Lemma l:l2_invariance and Lemma l:dual_nu_dens, used in Steps 1–3). The density condition does not imply (L1): e.g. p(x,y)=q(y) with q an unbounded L^2 probability density on (0,1) satisfies (e:Hs_condition_density) for every ell but violates (L1). So the two statements are not 'precisely' the same and the given proof does not cover the stated hypotheses. The same omission of (L1) occurs when cor:det_err_wendland and cor:det_err_matern invoke (e:hl_charac) without (L1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add hypothesis (L1) to thm:diff_density_hs_invariance (and to cor:det_err_wendland / cor:det_err_matern), or supply the direct Hilbert–Schmidt argument showing K: L^2 -> H^ell is bounded under (e:Hs_condition_density) without (L1).
issues.overall_effect: The Section 2 theorem is unsupported as written (though true, since with D_1^alpha p in L^2(Omega x Omega) the operator is Hilbert–Schmidt from L^2 into H^ell); the claim that it coincides with part (iii) is false; corollaries invoking (e:hl_charac) also silently need (L1).
issues.title: Density-based invariance theorem drops the (L1) hypothesis required by the result it invokes
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis addition or a short standard direct argument restores full validity with no loss of the advertised result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\bH\subset C_b(\Omega)$ be a RKHS that is invariant under $\calK$. Then $\calK : \bH\to\bH$ is bounded.
Again, this gives the boundedness of $\calK: H^\ell \to H^\ell$ by \Cref{prop:RKHS_inv}

issues.failure_explanation: Steps 1 and 2 derive boundedness of K on H^1 and H^ell from prop:RKHS_inv, which requires an RKHS continuously embedded in C_b. For n ≥ 2, H^1(Omega) (and H^ell for ell ≤ n/2) is not an RKHS and not contained in C_b, so the proposition's hypothesis is violated. Boundedness still follows from a closed-graph argument using L^2-boundedness (Lemma l:l2_invariance), but that argument is not given.

failure_location.quote: Then $\calK : H^1\to H^1$ is bounded by \Cref{prop:RKHS_inv}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the reference to prop:RKHS_inv by a closed-graph argument: if f_n -> f and K f_n -> g in H^ell, then both converge in L^2 and L^2-boundedness of K gives g = K f.
issues.overall_effect: The necessity direction of part (i) of thm:hs_frac_charac (invariance implies (e:hl_charac)) and the boundedness used in Step 3 rest on a misapplied result for general n; conclusions remain true with a replacement argument.
issues.title: Proposition prop:RKHS_inv applied to H^1 and H^ell, which are not RKHS when ell ≤ n/2
issues.why_classification: Routine local substitution of a standard closed-graph argument; all statements survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Condition (e:hl_charac) requires, for each |alpha| ≤ ell, a bound in the H^{-|alpha|} dual norm, i.e. |<D^alpha K f, phi>| ≤ C ||f||_{H^{|alpha|}} ||phi||_{L^2} for f in H^{|alpha|}. Repeating the Step 1 argument with H^ell in place of H^1 only yields |<D^alpha K f, phi>| ≤ ||K f||_{H^ell}||phi|| ≤ C||f||_{H^ell}||phi||, i.e. an H^{-ell} bound, which is strictly weaker for |alpha| < ell. Establishing the H^{-|alpha|} bound needs invariance/boundedness of K on each intermediate H^j (obtainable by the interpolation of Step 3), which the proof does not invoke. (Similarly, Step 1 records the alpha = 0 term in H^{-1} instead of H^0, and Step 5 records bounds in H^{-ell} instead of H^{-|alpha|}, although the estimates actually written there do give the stronger norms.)

failure_location.quote: Replacing $H^1$ by $H^\ell$ in the arguments from step 1 from \eqref{eq:h1_bound} onward, we get \eqref{e:hl_charac} for $\ell \in \bN$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invoke the interpolation argument of Step 3 (L^2 and H^ell invariance imply H^j invariance and boundedness for 0<j<ell) before Step 2, then apply the Step 1 estimate with H^{|alpha|} in place of H^1 for each alpha.
issues.overall_effect: The 'only if' half of the characterization in part (i) for ell ≥ 2 is not established as written; parts (ii) and (iii) (sufficiency) are unaffected.
issues.title: Necessity of (e:hl_charac) for ell ≥ 2 proved only in H^{-ell}-norms, not the required H^{-|alpha|}-norms
issues.why_classification: A short reordering of the paper's own interpolation argument closes the gap without changing any statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, condition \eqref{e:Hs_condition_density} is satisfied with $C = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left(1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi} C_1}\right)$.

issues.failure_explanation: With p = G/H and ∂_1 G = (y−x)G, the quotient rule gives ∂_1 p = G((y−x)/H − H'/H^2); the displayed formula omits the factor 1/H in the first term. The subsequent bound also uses 1/C_1 where the term H'/H^2 requires 1/C_1^2, and the claimed constant C ignores the |alpha| = 0 term ||p||_{L^2} required by the sum in (e:Hs_condition_density). The qualitative conclusion (bounded ∂_1 p, hence (e:Hs_condition_density) holds) is nevertheless true.

failure_location.quote: \partial_1 p(x,y) = \frac{\partial_1 G(x,y) H(x) - G(x,y) H'(x)}{H(x)^2} = G(x,y) \left( (y-x) - \frac{H'(x)}{H(x)^2}\right)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the formula to G((y−x)/H − H'/H^2), bound it by (1/√(2π))(1/C_1 + 1/(√(2π) C_1^2)), and include the ||p||_{L^2} term in C.
issues.overall_effect: The stated derivative and explicit constant are wrong; the invariance conclusion of the proposition survives.
issues.title: Erroneous derivative formula and constant in the truncated-normal example
issues.why_classification: Purely local recomputation; the proposition's conclusion is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega\subset\R^n$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary

issues.failure_explanation: The paper works on Ω ⊂ R^n for general n, yet asserts H^1 ⊂ C_b with continuous embedding. For n ≥ 2, H^1(Ω) contains unbounded, discontinuous functions (Sobolev embedding into C_b needs s > n/2, as the paper itself notes), so H^1 ⊄ C_b and consequently the finite measures M are not contained in H^{-1}. Also C_b(Ω)^* for open Ω is strictly larger than the finite regular signed measures on Ω.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the chain to n = 1 (or replace H^1 by H^s with s > n/2 and C_b^* by an appropriate measure space).
issues.overall_effect: A false background statement in the Sobolev recap; no result of the paper uses it.
issues.title: False inclusion chain H^1 ⊂ C_b ⊂ … ⊂ H^{-1} for general dimension
issues.why_classification: Isolated expository misstatement with no downstream use; trivially corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let the assumptions of \Cref{thm:total_error_bound} hold and let $\lambda \geq 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The deterministic part of (eq:reg_total_err_wendland) is obtained from (eq:det_error_tikhonov), which carries the factor (1+||K||_{H→H}); the Wendland bound absorbs it into C_1 but then asserts C_1 depends only on the kernel, which is false (it depends on ||K||_{H→H} and on Ω). In addition, the corollary is stated for λ ≥ 0 while the bound contains √(d/λ), which is undefined at λ = 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State C_1 = C(1+||K||_{H→H}) with C depending on k_{n,l} and Ω, and require λ > 0 (or fall back to thm:total_err_wendland for λ = 0).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised independence of C_1 from the dynamics is unsupported and the λ = 0 case is ill-posed; the qualitative bound is otherwise correct.
issues.title: Regularized Wendland bound claims constants independent of the Koopman operator and allows λ = 0
issues.why_classification: Only the description of the constant and a degenerate parameter value need adjusting; rate and structure are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives the rate h^{⌊ν⌋} from Wendland's Theorem 11.13, which needs the kernel to be C^{2⌊ν⌋}. For integer ν the Matérn function r^ν K_ν(r) is not C^{2ν} (e.g. ν = 1: r K_1(r) ≈ 1 + (r^2/2) log(r/2)+…, which is C^1 but not C^2), so the invoked smoothness hypothesis fails and Theorem 11.13 only gives h^{ν−1} in that case. The stated rate h^{⌊ν⌋} is still true, but only via the Sobolev-type estimate (Wendland Thm 11.17 with native space H^{ν+n/2}), which yields h^ν and is not the argument given; the remark attributing the Wendland kernels' extra 1/2 to compact support is likewise an artefact of the weaker theorem used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the C^{2⌊ν⌋}/Theorem 11.13 argument by the native-space Sobolev estimate (Wendland Thm 11.17), which gives the (better) rate h^ν for all ν > n/2-compatible parameters, or restrict the differentiability claim to non-integer ν.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of cor:det_err_matern (and hence the deterministic part of cor:total_error_bound_matern and cor:reg_total_err_bound_matern) is invalid for integer ν; the conclusion holds with a different justification.
issues.title: Matérn projection-error bound relies on a false smoothness claim for integer ν
issues.why_classification: A standard replacement citation repairs the proof and even improves the rate; nothing advertised is lost.
